title: Lasso — Operator Overview
description: Day-two operations: client completion versus upstream attempts, latency, failovers, head evidence, circuit recovery, WebSocket delivery and BEAM pressure. Node-wide panels are explicitly marked; missing data stays missing.

panels.title: Healthy exporters
panels.description: Scraped nodes whose bounded metrics observer is available. Compare with desired replicas. Missing data is unavailable, not a healthy zero.

panels.title: Unready chains
panels.description: Profile/chains with no eligible HTTP route or fresh head from that eligible set. Uses the same evidence as /api/ready. Missing data is unknown, not healthy.

panels.title: Client completion success
panels.description: Final routed completion ratio after failover. Defaults to client traffic; choose system to inspect probes. Excludes invalid/local ingress paths.

panels.title: Routed completions / sec
panels.description: Final completions, not individual attempts. Requests with missing origin are kept under unknown.

panels.title: Open HTTP circuits
panels.description: Counts node-local open circuits. One provider can count once per replica. An open circuit with healthy alternatives is reduced redundancy, not a proxy outage.

panels.title: Client latency — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: End-to-end routed duration includes failed attempts and retries. Seconds; sum buckets across nodes before computing quantiles. No traffic produces gaps.

panels.title: Completion rate by outcome
panels.description: Final outcomes. Probe failures do not dilute client success unless system origin is selected.

panels.title: Routing & upstreams — where is time or redundancy being lost?
Upstream attempt rate
panels.description: Every dispatched attempt, including ones recovered by later failover. Compare with completion rate to spot retry amplification.

panels.title: Successful upstream I/O p95
panels.description: Successful attempt latency by transport. Timeouts/cancellations are censored observations and excluded from this latency comparison.

panels.title: Attempt failures by category
panels.description: Timeout, capacity rejection, service failure, neutral error and cancellation remain distinct. Error text is never a label.

panels.title: Failovers per completed request
panels.description: Uses final request failover count. More than zero can indicate successful protection with upstream degradation.

panels.title: Fresh evidence and eligible alternatives
panels.description: 1 means fresh lag evidence is available; 0 means absent/expired observation. This is evidence availability, not full routing eligibility. Missing series means route/node unavailable.

panels.title: Head lag — blocks
panels.description: Compare with the configured max_lag_blocks for this chain. Missing evidence is not zero lag; use the evidence panel alongside this one.

panels.title: Circuit state
panels.description: One-hot local HTTP circuit state. Multiple replicas can disagree temporarily during recovery.

panels.title: Recovery delay remaining
panels.description: Remaining local recovery delay; no forced reset is needed for a normal upstream outage.

panels.title: Circuit transitions — node wide
panels.description: Physical upstream circuit events across selected nodes. Profile/chain/provider filters do not apply; use provider_info to join instance_id when diagnosing one upstream.

panels.title: Admission / failover events
panels.description: Includes system probes and legacy events without profile context. Choose profile/provider All to inspect those unknown-label events. Admission rejection does not mean an upstream received a request.

panels.title: HTTP ingress rate by route/status
panels.description: Node-wide endpoint requests including local, invalid, dashboard, and /metrics traffic. Paths are normalized and never include wallets or URL parameters.

panels.title: HTTP ingress p95
panels.description: Node-wide Phoenix endpoint duration. Includes local methods and validation failures that never dispatch upstream.

panels.title: WebSocket connection churn
panels.description: Connection/disconnection events, not an active subscription count. Unknown profile may occur in physical connection events.

panels.title: Subscription recovery / loss
panels.description: Failover, canonical repair, orphaned events, dropped events and slow-consumer termination. Subscription IDs and filters are never metric labels.

panels.title: Subscription recovery p95
panels.description: Completed failover and reorg repair durations. Missing data means no completed repairs in the window.

panels.title: Stream memory envelope — node wide
panels.description: Combined ingress, replay history and downstream delivery reservations. Different from OS RSS and BEAM total memory. Snapshots update every 10 seconds without a dashboard subscriber.

panels.title: Buffered messages — node wide
panels.description: Queued admitted messages retained for delivery or internal processing.

panels.title: Stream admission losses — node wide
panels.description: Admission losses indicate a bounded-memory protection triggered. Inspect slow consumers and reservations before raising limits.

panels.title: BEAM memory by allocation
panels.description: Categories overlap; do not sum total with its components. Use Kubernetes/cAdvisor for container RSS, requests and limits.

panels.title: Run queue vs online schedulers
panels.description: Sustained run-queue pressure is a useful overload signal. Does not pretend to be measured CPU utilization.

panels.title: Process / atom / port utilization
panels.description: Fractions of VM-configured limits, not arbitrary generic alert thresholds.

panels.title: GC collections / sec
panels.description: Observe alongside binary/process memory and latency. Counters reset on VM restart.

panels.title: Observer row utilization
panels.description: Bounded observer storage occupancy. Histograms export several time series per row. The legacy request counter has its own independent 4096-row cap.

panels.title: Metric observations dropped / invalid
panels.description: Any losses mean charts are incomplete; investigate series occupancy or an emitter contract mismatch.

panels.title: Credential health transitions — node wide
panels.description: Managed upstream authentication failures and recoveries over the selected window. Counts transitions, not current active alerts.

panels.title: VM uptime
panels.description: Use drops to explain counter resets. All counters are local and reset when their owner/node restarts.

panels.title: Collection availability / config scan truncation
panels.description: Node-wide exporter health. Available=1 is healthy. Route/chain truncation=1 means configured inventory exceeded the bounded scrape cap; some routes or chains are omitted.
